newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - H-P sees boost from Cisco.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - H-P sees boost from Cisco.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co Chairman and Chief Executive Lewis Platt on Wednesday said his company expected its collaboration with Cisco Systems Inc to improve its financial performance beginning this year.
"We expect to benefit during 1997," he told Reuters in an interview after a joint announcement at Cisco's headquarters.

Platt and Cisco Chief Executive John Chambers both said they expected the deal to result in added revenues for both companies, but they declined to elaborate on the size and timing of expected financial benefits.

"We are neither one of us growing at a rate as fast as we could if we provide this," Chambers said of the alliance, formed to develop Internet-ready networking offerings that combine the network and computer technology.

"Do we think our win rate will go up? Our answer is yes," said Chambers. "Our customers are saying to us, 'You've got to provide total worldwide support and service...You've got to provide better network management and integrate that into better enterprise and workgroup management.'"
Both executives said the deal would not be exclusive, but the collaboration would speed time to market.

With the fast pace of Internet development, time to market is a key issue. Hewlett-Packard is now moving quickly to help major corporate customers apply Internet technology both for using the global computer network and for developing intranets -- private computer networks that use Internet standards.
Cisco Systems is the market leader in internetworking systems, and both companies said it is increasingly important to integrate computers more closely into network technology.
"Networking and computers can no longer evolve along separate paths," said Charlie Giancarlo, Cisco Systems' vice president of business development.
The companies said the deal is an expansion of a collaboration between them over several years, including worldwide support, solution integration and technology collaboration efforts.
Executives said the companies expect products to be introduced soon, especially in hubs and networking solutions.
Work on network security, quality of service, computer chips and network managment technologies will follow, as well as greater product integration, services and support.

Chambers and Platt said it was difficult to quantify any specific financial benefits, although Chambers noted that Cisco's revenues in Japan have risen from $40 million a year slightly more than two years ago to more than $50 million a month as a result of partnership deals in that country.

"I expect that our revenue for our company will be better than it would have been without this alliance, but I'm not going to put a number on it," Platt said. "I want to be very concrete about it: We expect benefits during 1997."
